Donald Trump on Saturday put pressure on the US senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas to support a bill to make daylight saving time permanent, urging Americans to call what appeared to be the personal cellphone number of his fellow Republican and the chair of the Senate intelligence committee.

The Sunshine Protection Act passed the House in July, but it faces roadblocks in the Senate, where some Republicans are strongly opposed to it. Proponents, including the president and his administration, argue that the change would provide more daylight during the times that Americans are most active. Detractors said permanent daylight saving time would lead to darker and potentially more hazardous winter mornings when children will be waiting for school buses and parents will be driving to work in darkness.

item.description:
Yemeni forces say strikes conducted against Houthi targets in Sanaa, Saada

Yemen's armed forces said early on Sunday it was conducting strikes against the Houthis in the capital Sanaa and the group's stronghold Saada.

A spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, which are aligned with the internationally recognised government, said forces were targeting what he described as "vital targets", without providing further details.

Yemen's Houthi-run Al Masirah TV reported earlier an attack it said was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Sanaa. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation on the report.

The conflict between the Iran-backed Houthis and forces aligned with the Saudi-backed government mostly stopped after a 2022 truce, but fighting has broken out again in a spillover from the wider war between Iran and the United States.

Hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces also made major territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast.

Saudi Arabia has responded with air strikes in Yemen and backed government forces fighting to repel the Houthis.

item.description:

Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, has warned the United Arab Emirates (UAE) against challenging Tehran and its sovereignty over three islands in the Persian Gulf.

In a post on his X account, Velayati dismissed recent claims made by the UAE at the United Nations General Assembly regarding sovereignty over Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb, and Abu Musa, saying the three islands will remain Iranian forever, according to IRNA. 

"A country whose political life does not reach half a century makes claims from the UN podium about islands that have been recorded under Iran's name in historical documents and maps of past centuries," Velayati said in the Farsi-language post.

He added that the UAE should not "rely on foreign powers" for its security and should instead pursue good relations with its neighbours, IRNA reported.

"The neighbour stays, and the guest goes… Regional experience has shown that imported security has an expiration date," said the former Iranian foreign minister.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Hegseth: US blockade of Hormuz ironclad, Iran should make right choice
item.description:
Hegseth: US blockade of Hormuz ironclad, Iran should make right choice

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said that the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is “ironclad” and that US President Donald Trump has “all the options he needs on the table” if Iran continues to “play games” with the strait, according to an AP report carried by the Times of Israel.

“Iran wants to play games with things like the Strait of Hormuz. They don’t control it, we do,” Hegseth told reporters.

“They have literally gotten nothing through. Our blockade has been ironclad and we’re running almost at prewar levels every single night through that, you see that as far as the throughput.”

He added: “So we feel like we’re in a very strong position. Iran ought make the right choice. If they don’t, the president is going to have all the options he needs on the table. But he is not going to let these things extend unnecessarily. He understands what the mission is and we can get it done when called upon.”

Hegseth also said that Trump is “hellbent” on Iran not having a nuclear weapon, the report said.

“The message is very simple: Iran will never ever ever have a nuclear weapon. President Trump is hell-bent and determined to ensure that they do not; they will not,” Hegseth said.

item.description:
Israeli forces, settlers continue campaign of detentions and attacks in West Bank

Several Palestinians were detained by Israeli forces, while settlers continued attacks on Palestinian homes in the occupied West Bank since Saturday evening, according to reports.

* Israeli forces detained three Palestinian farmers and seized a truck loaded with bananas in the Ras al-Ahmar area, southeast of Tubas, according to Mutaz Basharat, the Tubas governorate official in charge of the Jordan Valley file, Wafa reported.

*Israeli settlers, protected by Israeli soldiers, attacked Palestinian homes on Saturday evening in the Wadi al-Hasin and Harat Jaber areas of Hebron’s Old City, south of the occupied West Bank. The assailants shouted threats and insults and used obscene language, Wafa reported. Israeli forces also fired live ammunition toward Palestinian homes in the area.

*Israeli settlers attacked and wounded a 27-year-old Palestinian man in the village of Usarin, south of Nablus. Medical sources told Wafa that the injured man was transferred to a hospital for treatment.

*Israeli forces launched an arrest campaign in the village of Burqa, in the Nablus district, north of the West Bank, Al Jazeera reported.

*Israeli forces raided the homes of Palestinian residents of the town of Kafr Qaddum, east of Qalqilya, while settlers attacked a home near Najah Hospital, north of Nablus city, according to Al Jazeera.

item.description:
Iran opens military centre for citizens, 'training 1,000 battalions'

Iran opened a military training centre in Tehran on Saturday, which is said to be aimed at preparing citizens to confront US and Israeli forces in the event of a ground attack.

 US-Israeli attacks on 28 February triggered seven months of conflict. A truce on 8 April halted 40 days of war, but sporadic hostilities continued.

The new centre at Haft-e Tir Square followed a first camp at Imam Hussein Square, hoping to train civilians in the coming weeks.

Footage from the centre showed army members conducting drills with camouflage-painted anti-aircraft equipment, crossing obstacle courses and using virtual reality headsets to train with weapons.

At a news conference, Ali Kowsari, deputy for training at the Basij organisation, said 1,000 battalions had been prepared for training. Kowsari stressed the importance of civil defence across society.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] NAZA: Israeli embassies in UK and US promote rival documentary to challenge Gaza genocide allegations
item.description:
NAZA: Israeli embassies in UK and US promote rival documentary to challenge Gaza genocide allegations

Submitted by MEE staff on Sun, 10/04/2026 - 03:02
The rival film’s directors remain unnamed for 'security reasons' while its website lists Three Musketeers Production as 'a company in formation'
Rachel Szor and Yuval Abraham on stage at the NAZA premiere during the 64th New York Film Festival at Alice Tully Hall in New York City, on 26 September 2026 (AFP/Dimitrios Kambouris)
Off

Israeli embassies in the United States and the United Kingdom are promoting a copycat NAZA, nearly a month after the release of the original that focuses on testimony of Israelis killing Palestinians in Gaza.

In posts on X, the embassies said that "Naza: The Real Story" is "setting the record straight" and claims to offer a firsthand account from senior Israeli military commanders and intelligence officers directly involved in Israel's genocidal war on Gaza. 

It said the film uses combat footage, declassified materials, captured intelligence and firsthand testimony to give context on "how the war was fought and the challenges Israeli forces faced".

The film's website names the provider as Three Musketeers Production, "a company in formation", and says a registered address and registration number will be published once the company is registered. It says the directors are deliberately not named "for their safety". 

Claimed to have been filmed on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the 49-minute documentary is available in 17 languages on its official website.

"Rooftop interviews with senior IDF [Israeli army] commanders: Hamas fighters in civilian clothes, hostages held in homes, aid and Hamas. For people about to watch this film, not a NASA picture," reads a blog entry about the film. 

The website lists a release date of 20 September 2026 and says the film will also be shown in theatres.

Blog posts on the film's website, dated 18-26 September, summarise interviews it says are included in the documentary. 

"One interview covers Gaza from north to south. No personal names appear on this page, and the directors are unnamed for security reasons," the website notes.

"This page summarises what the interviewee says. It reports his account and the IDF rules he describes. It does not verify them independently."

'Hang the traitors'

Directed by Israeli journalists Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, NAZA: A Window into Systems of Mass Killing has riled the Israeli government and far-right elements of Israeli society since its premiere and Special Jury Prize win at the Venice International Film Festival last month.

The 25-minute standing ovation for the film set a new record for any movie at a major festival, surpassing the near 24 minutes by The Voice of Hind Rajab at last year's Venice festival.

As elections loom, Naza controversy strikes at the heart of Israel's crisis
Read More »

NAZA examines the AI-powered systems used in Israel's war on Gaza and allegations that high numbers of Palestinian civilian deaths were factored into military targeting decisions.

The documentary features interviews with 24 Israeli military and intelligence insiders, whose identities remained anonymous.

Israeli politicians, journalists and members of the public have attacked Szor and Abraham, accusing them of treason and calling for their citizenship to be revoked.

Last month, Culture Minister Miki Zohar called the film "despicable" and said he would "act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators on the grounds of treason against the state".

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu joined Zohar in attacking the filmmakers, saying he would introduce two bills targeting those who "defame" the Israeli military. 

Netanyahu said the first bill "would revoke the citizenship of anyone who defames soldiers", while the second would increase "twentyfold the amount in damages for which they can be sued for defamation".

"They have no place among us," Netanyahu said of those who "defame" the Israeli army.

NAZA review: Portrait of Israel as a nation stuck in a moral abyss
Read More »

The Israeli military's Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir has ordered legal action against Szor and Abraham with the help of the Shin Bet, according to Israeli media.

Dozens of far-right Israelis gathered outside Szor's family home on 16 September, demanding she be hanged.

The Israeli newspaper Haaretz reported that several of the protesters demanded the "death penalty for traitors".

One demonstrator said that when Szor and Abraham return to Israel, "they should be tried and go to the gallows, and the family should be expelled and the house sealed".

Many social media users dismissed the documentary as "propaganda" and an attempt to "bury the real film".

An X account named Britain United wrote: "Pathetic, that actual Naza documentary must be really exposing for you to try to SEO bury the real film online by using the same title."

"You can try and spin the Israeli slaughter of the residents of Gaza all you want, but it won't work," X user Joe said.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Gaza Friendly: the French label turning consumer choices into Palestine solidarity
item.description:
Gaza Friendly: the French label turning consumer choices into Palestine solidarity

Submitted by Tassa Adidi on Mon, 09/28/2026 - 15:10
In France, a unique app certifies shopkeepers boycotting products linked to Israeli settlements while promoting alternative brands
Gaza Friendly, launched in 2025, is inspired by the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions movement (provided)
Off

Among the many apps available on the Play Store, one stands out thanks to its heart‑shaped icon featuring a Palestinian flag: “Gaza Friendly”.

Created in June 2025, the label certifies shopkeepers involved in the boycott of products originating from the occupied Palestinian territories and marketed by companies supporting Israel’s settlement expansion.

To date, the app and its associated website list 80 businesses in France, mainly butchers, restaurants, bakeries, caterers, tea rooms and food distributors.

The list is updated regularly, and the app features an interactive map allowing consumers to locate certified shops near their homes.

The app, which has been downloaded more than 500 times so far, was created by Pierre-Amael Noailly Charny, a paediatrician of Tunisian origin from Lyon, in east-central France, along with a small group of friends.

Noailly Charny explains that shopkeepers who join Gaza Friendly can express their commitment to the Palestinian cause in a concrete way.

‘This label gives people outraged by the genocide in Gaza the possibility to turn their consumption into a lever for justice and solidarity’

- Pierre-Amael Noailly Charny, founder of Gaza Friendly 

“The existence of this label gives people outraged by the genocide in Gaza the possibility to turn their consumption into a lever for justice and solidarity,” Noailly Charny told Middle East Eye.

The label draws inspiration from the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement, an international campaign launched in 2005 by Palestinian civil society to encourage consumers and institutions to refuse to buy Israeli products or goods originating from Israeli settlements, which are illegal under international law.

“Boycott works because refusing certain products cuts off resources from the oppression,” Gaza Friendly argues on its homepage, with the ambition of building a strong network of certified shopkeepers to give greater visibility to the boycott campaign.

‘My business is doing better’

To be certified, shopkeepers must comply with a three‑point charter: no Coca‑Cola Company beverages, no PepsiCo beverages, and no fresh products imported from Israeli settlements.

For Noailly Charny, boycotting Coca‑Cola and PepsiCo is a peaceful tool with strong symbolic impact, given their documented involvement in the illegal occupation of Palestinian territories.

In 2025, BDS revealed that Coca‑Cola operates a regional distribution centre and refrigerated warehouses in the settlement of Atarot in the West Bank, while PepsiCo is targeted for investments and subsidiaries linked to Israel.

‘The idea appealed to me, especially since some customers had already blamed me for selling Coca‑Cola’

- Akli, Gaza Friendly‑certified shopkeeper

Although PepsiCo maintains it does not support Israel politically or militarily, activists argue that its ownership of Israeli brands SodaStream and Sabra, along with its operations in the country, amount to indirect support for the Israeli state. Coca‑Cola, for its part, insists that it does not endorse any country, government or policy, but has not addressed the allegations concerning the Atarot facility.

Both companies declined to respond to MEE’s request for comment.

“Even before Gaza Friendly existed, some shopkeepers had already taken the initiative to stop selling Coca‑Cola and Pepsi products. We therefore chose to put them in the spotlight and list them to set an example and encourage others to join,” Noailly Charny said.

Aid Boucherie Halal in Creteil, near Paris, is one of the latest certified businesses. Its name appeared on the Gaza Friendly list on 4 September. Akli, the owner, says he heard about the label through an acquaintance.

“The idea appealed to me, especially since some customers had already blamed me for selling Coca‑Cola. Personally, I didn’t know the company had interests in Israel,” he told MEE.

Akli says he has always been supportive of Palestinians but didn’t know how to express that support.

“Now I don’t sell Coca-Cola or Pepsi, and my business is doing just as well - actually, even better,” he said, noting a slight increase in customer numbers.

Solidarity brands

In addition to listing shopkeepers, Gaza Friendly provides them with visual materials such as posters and stickers to improve visibility. It also offers a non‑exhaustive list of alternative products, particularly beverages, to replace brands targeted by the boycott.

Some of these drinks come from companies committed to Palestine. This is the case for Pales Drinks, a Belgian brand of sodas created in 2024 by young entrepreneur Abdelhakim Tarnach, which donates 10 percent of its profits to humanitarian actions in Palestine.

Watermelon Index names and shames companies complicit in Israel's war on Gaza
Read More »

The same year saw the launch of Palestine Cola, a soft drink marketed by Safad Food AB, a company founded by entrepreneurs of Palestinian origin based in Malmo, Sweden.

Here too, part of the profits from the sale of cans - decorated with an olive tree and wrapped in a keffiyeh pattern - funds emergency aid projects in Palestine such as clothing, tents and food assistance.

In France, Palestine Cola is mainly distributed by Jebalia, an online retailer promoting alternative, ethical and solidarity‑based consumption. On its Instagram page, each purchase is presented as an act of support for humanitarian causes.

Since July, Jebalia has been listed among Gaza Friendly‑certified businesses. Its owner Sofiane Slimani proudly embraces his commitment to Palestine.

“We’ve reached a point where boycotting products linked to Israeli settlement activity is no longer enough. We need to offer alternatives,” he told MEE.

Jebalia claims to have sold 100,000 cans of soda in 2025, its founding year. Beyond social media, the company uses other communication channels to make itself known.

‘We’ve reached a point where boycotting products linked to Israeli settlement activity is no longer enough. We need to offer alternatives’

- Sofiane Slimani, Gaza Friendly‑certified retailer

It was present at the latest edition of the Annual Gathering of Muslims of France in Le Bourget last April and regularly partners with engaged businesses to offer its drinks at solidarity events, such as the charity football tournament Salam Cup held a few months ago in Bobigny, near Paris.

During this event supporting Palestine, Jebalia products were sold by Inda Coffee, a French coffee shop and matcha bar supporting aid initiatives for Gaza.

Although involved in the boycott campaign, Inda Coffee is not yet certified by Gaza Friendly. According to Noailly Charny, many shopkeepers still don’t know the label exists - hence the need, he insists, for more publicity.

“We’re trying to reach influencers who work in the food sector,” the paediatrician said. In Lyon, AmarFood, a content creator specialising in gastronomy and halal, alcohol‑free restaurants in Lyon and the Paris region, often promotes Gaza Friendly in his videos.

More recently, another videographer shared a story in which he explained the concept at length.

Beyond France, Gaza Friendly aims to expand internationally. Shopkeepers from around 15 countries are already members of the label, which has no equivalent anywhere else in the world.

In a separate attack, Saqr al-Qaisi was killed when an Israeli drone struck a vehicle in the city's al-Hawouz area.

Meanwhile, in southern Gaza, Israeli shelling continues to pound Khan Younis's Sheikh Nasser neighbourhood.

Al Jazeera reports that in Gaza City, several people have been wounded in an Israeli drone strike near the Abd al-Rahman School in al-Saftawi in the city's north, while another person was shot in the Tuffah neighbourhood. The Israeli military also conducted demolitions in the city's east.

Israeli military vehicles also opened fire east of al-Qarara, north of Khan Younis, and north of Beit Lahiya.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Tanker hit by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
item.description:
Tanker hit by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says

A tanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, causing damage to its engine room, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Sunday, without specifying when the incident occurred.

The crew was safe and no environmental impact had been reported at the time the notice was issued, UKMTO added.

Reporting by Reuters

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] NAZA: Israeli embassies in UK and US promote rival documentary to challenge Gaza genocide allegations
item.description:
NAZA: Israeli embassies in UK and US promote rival documentary to challenge Gaza genocide allegations

Israeli embassies in the United States and the United Kingdom are promoting a copycat NAZA, nearly a month after the release of the original that focuses on testimony of Israelis killing Palestinians in Gaza.

In posts on X, the embassies said that "Naza: The Real Story" is "setting the record straight" and claims to offer a firsthand account from senior Israeli military commanders and intelligence officers directly involved in Israel's genocidal war on Gaza. 

It said the film uses combat footage, declassified materials, captured intelligence and firsthand testimony to give context on "how the war was fought and the challenges Israeli forces faced".

The film's website names the provider as Three Musketeers Production, "a company in formation", and says a registered address and registration number will be published once the company is registered. It says the directors are deliberately not named "for their safety". 

Claimed to have been filmed on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the 49-minute documentary is available in 17 languages on its official website.

Read more: NAZA: Israeli embassies in UK and US promote rival documentary to challenge Gaza genocide allegations
